original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write a complete operation alphabet outside one named premise and price a baseline before searching identities.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.

actual_scope: Balanced (5 a-labels, 5 b-labels) ten-call words for T = diag([S],[S],[S],[S]) at exactly r = 4 in the formal F2[GL_2(F2)] rank-one-idempotent register model, via the proposed J^2-coefficient-layer expansion in F2[G]/J^3 plus a bounded exact full-formal search over the balanced profile.
scope_change_reason: The card permits a fixed larger register count. This is the named residual of the four-SWAP r=4 line: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1705 narrows the minimum to q in {8,10,12}; the concurrent saturation claim https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1715 explicitly leaves 'the ten-call balanced case' outside its session; and the handoff https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18918391 names the J^2-layer bound in F2[G]/J^3 as a smallest useful next task.
bottleneck_link: A balanced ten-call word would price four coordinate-SWAP targets below the 12-call direct bill inside the bit register model; scalar or partial words alone change nothing, and no kappa or selected-supplier change follows either way.
stop_rule: One bounded seeded search pass at the stated budget (6,000,000 conditioned samples), one route decision: if the J^3 layer cannot separate the balanced profile, record the exact obstruction and stop the layer route rather than raising the budget.
evidence: research/four-swap-balanced-j3-layer/verify.py exact bit arithmetic: augmentation dims (5,4,4) with J^2 = J^3 so R/J^3 is the sign quotient F2[z]/(z^2); the layer equation is machine-checked equivalent to sum N_i = I_r (200/200 random instances); expansion identity prod(1+eps) = 1 + sum eps + sum_{i<j} eps_i eps_j mod J^3 checked on seeded random words; four direct control words (3/6/9/12 calls) hit their targets; four mutation controls fail; r=1 and r=2 balanced search controls find known witnesses; 6,000,000 conditioned samples (22,903 valid tuples x 252 labelings = 5,771,556 exact M_4(F2[G]) checks) find no balanced ten-call word realizing the target.
author: Aaron Wang

open_questions.question: Can the balanced (5,5) ten-call profile realize T = diag([S],[S],[S],[S]) at r = 4 at all, now that the J^3 layer is known to be vacuous for it?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only sub-12 four-SWAP candidate left once label saturation is proved, so it decides whether the four-SWAP minimum is 10 or 12.
open_questions.first_step: Use the surviving full-word structure instead of the augmentation layer: the natural 2-dimensional image in M_8(F2), or an order-sensitive invariant from the commutator [([a]+1),([b]+1)] = [ab]+[ba] in J^2, on the same balanced domain.
open_questions.blocked_by: J^2 = J^3 in F2[G], so no second augmentation layer exists; any further exclusion must use word order or a different quotient of F2[G].

open_questions.question: Does the balanced-profile obstruction at r = 4 persist at r = 5 with one restored dirty extra register?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the smallest falsifying instance of 'workspace cheapens the tariff' for four SWAP targets and tests whether register growth changes the picture.
open_questions.first_step: Rerun the same conditioned search at r = 5 with target diag([S] x 4, 1), conditioning on sum N_i = diag(I_4, 0): the restored fifth role carries the identity boundary, so its target augmentation is zero and the sign quotient forces diag(I_4, 0), not I_5 (corrected after review follow-up; the earlier I_5 wording would exclude every solution to that endpoint).
open_questions.blocked_by: The r = 5 balanced question itself is open; only the r = 4 balanced domain was searched here.
